paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the word of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Eze 6:2.
paragraphs.anchor: Set thy face.

paragraphs.text: Inhabited by the Edomites.
paragraphs.anchor: Against Mount Seir.

paragraphs.text: This had been done before, {Eze 25:12} but not enough. God hath a further saying to them, and that for the comfort of his poor people who might thus object. Peace and security from danger is promised us in the foregoing chapter; but we have still many deadly enemies, and none worse than our near allies and next neighbours the Edomites. Here, therefore, they are heavily threatened with utter desolation for their malignity against Israel, and their blasphemy against God.
paragraphs.anchor: And prophesy against it.

paragraphs.text: Ecce ego ad te; have at thee.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, O Mount Seir, I am against thee.

paragraphs.text: I will have my full blow at thee.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will stretch out my hand against thee.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Desolation and desolation. I will make an utter end; desolation shall not rise up the second time; {Nah 1:9} I will make short work. {Rom 9:28}
paragraphs.anchor: I will make thee most desolate.

paragraphs.text: Even Teman, Dedan, Bozrah, mentioned in Scripture; besides many others mentioned by geographers, Maresa, Rhinocorura, Raphia, Gaza, Anthedon, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: I will lay thy cities waste.

paragraphs.text: To thy small comfort.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt know.

paragraphs.text: A Lord of lords, a God of gods, "a great God, a mighty and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward." {Deu 10:17}
paragraphs.anchor: That I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: A hereditary deadly feud against Israel. Heb., An enemy of ages, yea, of many ages continuance; such as is, as we use to say of Runner, the older the stronger.
paragraphs.anchor: Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred.

paragraphs.text: Ut diffluant; hast let out their life blood: all malice is bloody.
paragraphs.anchor: And hast shed the blood of the children of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Watching the worst time to do them the most mischief.
paragraphs.anchor: In time of their calamity.

paragraphs.text: When I had in a manner done with them, yet thou hadst not done with them; but didst stir up Nebuzaradan to burn the city and temple with fire. This was to help forward the affliction. {Zec 1:15} {See Trapp on "Zec 1:15"}
paragraphs.anchor: In the time that their iniquity had an end.

paragraphs.text: Thou shalt have blood thy bellyful, which thou hast so greedily sought and sucked. Satiabis te sanguine quem sitiisti, cuiusque insatiabilis semper fuisti, as the Scythian queen said to Cyrus’s head.
paragraphs.anchor: I will prepare thee unto blood.

paragraphs.text: As a bloodhound. It shall, it shall, believe me it shall.
paragraphs.anchor: Even blood shall pursue thee.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 35:3. Iterum repetit, ne excidisse videatur. I am in good earnest.
paragraphs.anchor: Most desolate.

paragraphs.text: Oh the woe of war! The Greek word {a} for it signifies much blood.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will fill his mountains.

paragraphs.text: {a} πολεμος q. πολυαιμος. Bellum a belluis. War from wild beasts.
For thy perpetual hatred. {Eze 35:5}
paragraphs.anchor: I will make thee perpetual desolations.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 35:4.
paragraphs.anchor: And thy cities.

paragraphs.text: Ungodly men must answer for their ungodly speeches also. {Jdg 1:15}
paragraphs.anchor: Because thou hast said.

paragraphs.text: Israel and Judah.
paragraphs.anchor: These two nations.

paragraphs.text: Such was their avarice and ambition that they made account all was their own; they had in their hopes devoured these two countries which God had reserved for a better purpose. He kept the room empty till the return of the natives; and the land kept her sabbaths, resting from tillage, &c. And yet these miscreants added,
paragraphs.anchor: Shall be mine.

paragraphs.text: Or, Though it be a Jehovahshammah, as Eze 48:35; be it that the Lord is there - scil., to keep possession against us - we will out him, and have it in despite of him. O tongues worthy to be pulled out, cut in gobbets, and driven down their throats, that did thus blaspheme!
paragraphs.anchor: Whereas the Lord was there.

paragraphs.text: Let the Romish Edomites expect the like punishment: their malice and mischief will come home to them.
paragraphs.anchor: I will do even according to thine anger.

paragraphs.text: That quicksighted and sharp fanged malignity which none can stand before. {Pro 27:4}
paragraphs.anchor: And according to thine envy.

paragraphs.text: Of both sorts; those in the first table against myself, and those in the second table against my people.
paragraphs.anchor: And that I have heard all thy blasphemies.

paragraphs.text: And we have helped after.
paragraphs.anchor: They are laid desolate.

paragraphs.text: Heb., To devour. Nay, but stay till they be; and then know that ye may devour that on earth, that ye shall digest in hell.
paragraphs.anchor: They are given us to consume.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Magnified, setting your mouths against heaven, your tongues also have walked through the earth. {Psa 73:9; see the notes there}
paragraphs.anchor: Thus with your mouth ye have boasted.

paragraphs.text: When it would have better become you to have multiplied your words before me in prayer and praises, as the Hebrew word ( òúø) here used, mostly signifieth.
paragraphs.anchor: And have multiplied your words against me.

paragraphs.text: scil, For my people’s deliverances. Or, When the whole land, scil., of Israel, rejoiceth; as it is sometimes hale and well with the Church, when the wicked are in the suds. Judea was the world of the world, as Athens was the "Epitome of Greece," the "Greece of Greece."
paragraphs.anchor: When the whole earth rejoiceth

paragraphs.text: As thou wast sick of the devil’s disease, rejoicing at other men’s harms; so, by a strange turn of things, others shall rejoice at thy just destruction, and revel in thy ruins: and at the last day especially, when thou shalt be awarded thy portion with the devil and his angels. {2Th 1:6-8}
paragraphs.anchor: As thou didst rejoice.

paragraphs.text: This was accordingly effected shortly after by Nebuchadnezzar and his Chaldees, as Josephus {a} testifieth; and is daily executed on the Church’s enemies, who shall all be ere long in the place that is fittest for them - scil., under Christ’s feet.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt be desolate, O Mount Seir.

paragraphs.text: The Edomites, that thought of seizing on others’ lands, lost their own. They who covet all, do oft lose all; yea, even the pleasure of that they possess; as a greedy dog swalloweth the whole meat that is cast him, without any pleasure, as gaping still for the next morsel.
paragraphs.anchor: And all Idumea, even all of it.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. xii. cap. 11.
